subject: laser beam
title: Scientists Slowed Light to 38 Miles an Hour. Then They Stopped It

scenes.text: Light has been slowed to 38 miles an hour.
Normally it covers 186,000 miles every second. Nothing is faster.
In 1999 a Harvard team fired a laser pulse into a tiny cloud of sodium atoms.
The cloud had been chilled to a few billionths of a degree above absolute zero.
Inside it, light crawled along 20 million times slower than normal. A racing cyclist could have beaten it.
Two years later the same physicist went further. She brought light to a complete stop.

description:
Light has been slowed to 38 miles an hour.
In 1999 a Harvard team led by physicist Lene Hau sent laser pulses into a Bose-Einstein condensate, a cigar-shaped cloud of sodium atoms only about 10 by 100 microns across, cooled to a few billionths of a degree above absolute zero. The light passed through at 17 meters per second, about 38 mph, roughly 20 million times slower than its usual 186,000 miles per second. The result was published in Nature. In 2001 Hau became the first person to stop light completely.
What would you do with light you could hold still? Comment below.
first_comment: The 1999 paper is titled Light speed reduction to 17 metres per second in an ultracold atomic gas. What should we slow down next?
